summary: A function gives a name to a group of commands so you can run them many times with different arguments. Bash functions return text with echo and success or failure with an exit code.
notes: average prints 83, not 83.4, because $(( )) only does whole-number math and drops the decimal part.
is_passing has no echo. The exit code of its last command, [ "$1" -ge 70 ], is what if checks.
local total inside average is a separate variable, so the total="not set" outside the function is unchanged.
pitfall: return only sets an exit code from 0 to 255. return 92 does not give you 92 in a variable. Use echo inside the function and result=$(letter_grade 92) outside.
